messages:
alex_k: FYI customer reporting `go get` failing for our go SDK after they pulled the tagged release v1.4.0. error: "verifying module: checksum mismatch". happens only when GOPROXY is set.

maria_s: Can you paste the exact command and output?

alex_k: Repro steps from customer: `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer org go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v1.4.0`

alex_k: Output snippet they sent: ```
go: downloading github.com/redwood/inference-go v1.4.0
verifying github.com/redwood/inference-go@v1.4.0: checksum mismatch
	downloaded: h1:abcdef...
	sum.golang.org: h1:012345...
```

samir: Huh, checksum mismatch usually means tag contents changed after proxy saw it or the module zip differs (lightweight vs annotated?). Any chance the v1.4.0 tag was force-updated?

alex_k: Customer says they created a tag from CI; CI maybe pushed after a late go.mod tweak. Not sure if force-push happened.

maria_s: Quick checks: 1) can you `git ls-remote --tags` for their repo? 2) ask them to run `GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1 go get -x ...` to see exact zip URL.

eng_oncall: Also check if the tag is signed (gpg) or annotated. There's a known edge where some hosting serves a different archive shape for annotated tags which can change checksums.

support_lead: We should repro locally before escalating. alex_k, can you try with GOPROXY=proxy.golang.org and with GOPRIVATE pointing to their org? If it repros, capture `GOMODCACHE` zip.

alex_k: Trying now — repro on my box. same checksum mismatch. Running `go env` shows: ```
GOMODCACHE=/home/alex/go/pkg/mod
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,https://goproxy.io,direct
GONOSUMDB=github.com/customer
```

alex_k: I fetched the module zip URL shown in trace and unzip: I can see go.mod at root in the zip but commit id differs from tag commit. looks like proxy cached an earlier zip.

samir: If proxy cached earlier commit and tag was moved, sumdb/proxy will keep old checksum. Two safe fixes: 1) push a new semver tag (v1.4.1) with the same content as current head; or 2) instruct customers to use `GOSUMDB=off` and `GOPRIVATE`/`GONOSUMDB` but that weakens verification. Recommend new patch tag.

maria_s: Another option: if they must keep v1.4.0 tag name, they could create a new commit that matches the original tag zip and re-tag, but that's messy. Safer: publish v1.4.1.

alex_k: Customer says they prefer not to bump semver because downstream pinned v1.4.0. They asked if we can ask proxy to purge cache. Any way from our side?

eng_oncall: We cannot purge proxy.golang.org; only the module proxy operator can. For private proxies (artifactory, Athens) you can trigger a cache refresh. If the org uses a private GOPROXY, ask them to purge.

support_lead: For short-term workaround for CI, suggest `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@master` or `@<commit>` so CI uses a commit pseudo-version rather than cached tag. Also mention consequences.

alex_k: I replied with repro & suggested v1.4.1. Customer came back: they found the issue — their release job pushed an unsigned lightweight tag and then the release job amended commit (rewrote history) and re-pushed the same tag name. That explains checksum mismatch.

maria_s: Good find. Document resolution steps in case others hit this: 1) never force-update tags that are published; 2) prefer creating new semver tags for fixes; 3) if you must fix tag, coordinate proxy cache purge or push new tag.

samir: I'll open a short KB entry and a snippet for release pipelines to avoid rewriting tags. Will add CI check to fail if `git push --force` happens on a release branch.

devops-bot: created kb-354: "go module checksum mismatch after tag rewrite" and assigned to samir. :white_check_mark:

alex_k: Marking this thread resolved with customer, they've moved to v1.4.1 and CI green. Closing. :tada:
